T16: holding the three indices and the liquid ETF, a quarter each, when the three-index switch is OUT and the gold signal is SELL

Test T16, run headline; descriptive, no null, no chance claim (waiver); findings PROVISIONAL at most; pre-registration sha256 eda7321d73b71455; every table carries its own dates. Contents: answer, rules and runs in words, data, one backtest, D-table and ledger, results by regime, curves, robustness, definitions.

1. The answer

Question. In the weeks when the three-index switch (the weekly supertrends of Nifty 100, Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100) is OUT and the weekly MAUc1 gold signal is SELL (the OUT-SELL regime), does holding the three indices and the liquid ETF, 25% each, whatever the indices' own signals say, change what the switch earns, on both base sleeves (50/50 and 80/20) and on two windows? The comparisons are descriptive: the new holding against the original sleeve (CAGR and worst fall), against the liquid ETF alone, against half parent + half GOLDBEES and against T15's holding of only the indices that are still BUY (CAGR and worst fall), six comparisons per window and base, 24 in all (T16.md 2.3). Test T16, descriptive, no null.

19 of 24 comparisons pass (a pass = the stated sign in at least 3 of the books), after 20.8 bps, whole window; the verdict per window and base follows the table of rules and runs below.

The rules and the runs in words (read this first)

States, read every Friday: IN = the Nifty 100, Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 weekly supertrend SIGNs are all BUY (the book holds the parent's basket); otherwise the switch is OUT and the book holds a sleeve: OUT-BUY = OUT and the weekly MAUc1 gold SIGN is BUY; OUT-SELL = OUT and MAUc1 is SELL. B = the indices whose own SIGN is BUY in an OUT week and k = how many (0, 1 or 2; 3 would be IN). Base sleeve: 50 = 50% GOLDBEES / 50% cash; 80 = 80% GOLDBEES / 20% cash when gold is BUY and 20% / 80% when gold is SELL. Cash = the LBES liquid-ETF level. The ten rules differ only in what they hold in OUT-SELL. A rule id is <base>-<its OUT-SELL holding>, such as 50-all; a bare suffix (-orig, -half, -liq, -idx, -all) means that holding on both bases.

What this page can and cannot say. There is no null, no random draw, no percentile and no p-value in T16 (Manu's waiver, 2026-11-26), so no claim about chance or skill is made. A PASS means only that the stated difference had the stated sign in at least 3 of the 4 books over the seen weeks. The four books are one market seen four times: in OUT-SELL weeks -all holds the same four lines in every book, so their agreement is close to automatic. Both windows were seen before the variant was proposed (post-hoc), there is no hold-out, and choosing the best of the ten rules from these tables is a selection on seen data. Findings are PROVISIONAL at most (T16.md 2.2); the verdict wording below is the pre-registered outcome map (T16.md 2.5) applied mechanically.

The largest caveats (T16.md 3, known contaminants):

  • The index leg is a price index with no dividends and no fund cost, not a tradable instrument: a real index fund or ETF would differ by roughly the dividend yield minus its costs, and Smallcap 100 / Midcap 100 funds were thin or absent in 2014-2019. R5 tests the cost side only (0.5 pp a year); the dividend side is not run (no approved dividend series). -all puts 75% of the book in this leg in every OUT-SELL week.
  • The effective sample is the OUT-SELL spells (the independent unit for the change): W1 (T11's / T14's / T15's inputs): 8 OUT-SELL spells in 54 weeks (-idx holds an index in 6 of those spells); W2 (T08's inputs, extended): 8 OUT-SELL spells in 49 weeks (-idx holds an index in 7 of those spells).
  • The four books are one market seen four times, with one in-or-out series and one gold series; in OUT-SELL weeks -all holds identical indices and cash in all four, so "3 of 4" is a consistency check, not four tests.
  • W1's parent is rebuilt from the parent's baskets and Eikon prices, not validated against a published NAV before 2019-01-02 (no published series exists before 2019-01-02); nine manual Eikon exports for delisted stocks (provenance unrecorded) supply bars in W1; both windows are seen; the variant, the rule's weights and the MAUc1 signal were chosen after seeing 2014-2026 results; cash is a quarter of -all's regime holding, and the cash file's source before 2026-08-10 is unrecorded (F-AA-D09).
  • The extension of W2 to 2026-11-20: the index signals, index prices, MAUc1 and the 2026-11-23 GOLDBEES file were auto-approved on Manu's instruction, not reviewed by him; the eight T15 rules reproduce T15's W2 to 2026-10-30 (gate V4(a)); the last OUT-SELL spell of W2 ends at the window end and its open position is marked at the last close.

3. One backtest, end to end

One book (the first), one window at a time, rule 50-all at 20.8 bps, from the signals to the statistics, with the formulas and the real numbers from trades.csv: an entry into OUT-SELL, an exit, a week in which an index is on SELL and the rule holds it anyway, and a change of the BUY set that the rule does not trade. A reader with a calculator can redo every step. The trade rows are read from the evidence by a fixed rule (the first such trade of the book), and the page says which.

5. Results by regime (added after the results were read; descriptive)

Manu asked, after reading the results, for the results broken down by regime. These tables are not part of the frozen design, are descriptive only and post-hoc, and make no claim about chance: they say what each instrument and each rule did in the weeks each regime was held. Each weekly decision governs the span from the close of its trade session to the close of the next decision's trade session; a regime's figure compounds its spans. Growth over all the regime's weeks is the figure to read; the annualised rate is shown for scale and is inflated by short spans. Table A uses the first book's calendar for the instruments (SCMO_0007 starts two sessions later in W2). Generated by tests/T16/regime_basis.py; every number is re-derived by check_page.py.

6. The curves: the ten rules and the parent, per book

Growth of 1 invested at the close of the first session of the window, log scale, 20.8 bps, daily marks (every 5th session drawn; the hover reads the same arrays). Click a chip to show or hide that curve in all four charts of the window; the vertical axis rescales to the curves shown, and the hover lists only those. The page opens with the parent, 50-orig and 50-all. The two originals are dashed when drawn; the two -all rules are thick. Shaded by the state held (each switchable): green = IN (the parent), blue = OUT-BUY (the base sleeve), grey = OUT-SELL with k = 0 (every index on SELL: -all holds the three indices, -idx only cash), amber = OUT-SELL with k ≥ 1 (-idx holds an index too). A ratio chip draws the growth ratio of an -all rule over its -liq, -orig or -idx rule on a right-hand axis (above the dotted 1.0× line the -all rule is ahead); the end values of every curve are in each caption whether it is drawn or not.

7. Robustness R1-R5

R1: 0 and 50 bps; R2: LIQUIDCASE as the cash leg; R3: the window from 2015-01-02 (W1) or the live decisions from 2021-11-01 (W2); R4: one spell left out; R5: a fund-cost drag of 0.5 pp a year on the index leg. No variant is tested against chance.

8. Definitions, formulas and how to reproduce

nav

NAV_t = cash_t + Σ_i units_i × close_i,t over the parent's stocks, GOLDBEES and each of the three indices (Nifty 100, Midcap 100, Smallcap 100: units × the index close; on a calendar session with no index bar the last close is carried); cash = LBES units × LBES level; base 1.0 at the close of the first session; daily marks on the book's sessions; units are constant between trades

cost

at a trade session (the session after the decision), at its fill prices (stocks OHLC4, GOLDBEES de-spiked OHLC4, cash at its level, each index at its own OHLC4): V = value of every line; target value of line i = target share_i × V; traded = Σ over every line (stocks, GOLDBEES, cash, each index) |target value_i − held value_i|; cost = traded × cost_bps ÷ 2 ÷ 10,000 (10.4 bps a side at 20.8 bps; 0 and 50 bps as robustness); every target is then scaled by (V − cost) ÷ V, so line i after the trade = target share_i × (V − cost) units_i = value after ÷ fill price_i; shares after cost = value after ÷ (V − cost)

regime

at a weekly decision (the last session of each ISO week, and T0): the latest Master row of each index and of MAUc1 dated on or before the decision date; IN = all three index SIGNs BUY; OUT-BUY = not IN and MAUc1 SIGN BUY; OUT-SELL = not IN and MAUc1 SIGN SELL. B = the indices (Nifty 100, Midcap 100, Smallcap 100) whose own SIGN is BUY at the decision; k = |B| (at most 2 in OUT-SELL, since 3 BUY is IN). Only the -idx rules read B; the -all rules ignore it

targets

target shares of the book at a decision (parent / GOLDBEES / cash / each index): all rules, IN: parent 1. -orig, -liq, -half OUT: T14's (e, gw): parent e, GOLDBEES (1 − e) × gw, cash (1 − e) × (1 − gw); 50-orig OUT-BUY and OUT-SELL: GOLDBEES 0.5, cash 0.5; 80-orig: OUT-BUY GOLDBEES 0.8, cash 0.2, OUT-SELL GOLDBEES 0.2, cash 0.8; -liq OUT-SELL: cash 1; -half OUT-SELL: parent 0.5, GOLDBEES 0.5; -liq and -half OUT-BUY as the base sleeve. -idx (50-idx, 80-idx): IN parent 1; OUT-BUY the base sleeve; OUT-SELL: cash 1 ÷ (k + 1) and each index in B 1 ÷ (k + 1), no parent, no GOLDBEES. -all (50-all, 80-all): IN parent 1; OUT-BUY the base sleeve; OUT-SELL: cash 0.25, Nifty 100 0.25, Midcap 100 0.25, Smallcap 100 0.25 whatever B, no parent, no GOLDBEES. A trade is due on the session after decision j iff the target key differs from decision j − 1's; for -idx the key includes B (a change of B inside OUT-SELL is a trade); for -all the key is the regime alone, so only entries into and exits from OUT-SELL trade and the four lines drift in between

cagr

CAGR = NAV_end ^ (252 ÷ (sessions − 1)) − 1 (sessions = the book's trading sessions in the window; years = (sessions − 1) ÷ 252; arithmetic, price return, after the stated cost)

maxdd

max drawdown = min over t of ( NAV_t ÷ max(NAV_s, s ≤ t) − 1 ) (negative; 'shallower or equal' = closer to 0 or equal, by the unrounded value)

calmar

Calmar = CAGR ÷ |max drawdown|

vol

volatility = standard deviation (n − 1) of the daily NAV returns × √252

diff

difference = statistic(A) − statistic(B) on the same book, window, cost and cash leg; CAGR, max drawdown, volatility and cost paid in pp (a positive max-drawdown difference = shallower); Calmar as a number; trades as a count; cost paid = Σ of the costs of the run's trades as a share of the starting NAV 1.0, shown in pp

cmp

C1: CAGR(b-all) > CAGR(b-orig); C2: max drawdown(b-all) ≥ max drawdown(b-orig); C3: CAGR(b-all) > CAGR(b-liq); C4: CAGR(b-all) > CAGR(b-half); C5: CAGR(b-all) > CAGR(b-idx); C6: max drawdown(b-all) ≥ max drawdown(b-idx); by the unrounded statistics, per book, after 20.8 bps over the whole window. n = the number of books in which the condition holds; the comparison PASSES iff n ≥ 3 of the books. No null, no draws, no percentile, no p-value: a pass describes seen weeks and is not a claim about chance

ledger

ledger return of an instrument or rule over a span = value_end ÷ value_start − 1, from the close of the session on which the span's first decision is traded (T0 for decision 0) to the close of the session on which the decision that ends it is traded (or the last session); an OUT-SELL spell = a run of consecutive OUT-SELL decisions; a stretch = a run inside it with the same B (so the same k); parent = hold the parent (0 bps); Nifty 100, Midcap 100, Smallcap 100 = the hold-the-index NAV (index close ÷ index close); each rule = its own NAV at 20.8 bps; GOLDBEES and cash = close ÷ close from the evidence's ledger

rbasis

results by regime (added after the results were read): decision j governs the span from the close of the session on which it is traded (T0 for decision 0) to the close of the session on which decision j + 1 is traded (the last session for the last decision); the spans tile the window. A span's regime is its decision's: IN, OUT-BUY, OUT-SELL with k = 0 (every index on SELL) or with k ≥ 1. per regime and series X: sessions n = Σ span lengths; growth = Π over its spans of X_end ÷ X_start − 1; annualised = (1 + growth)^(252 ÷ n) − 1; log growth = Σ ln(X_end ÷ X_start); weeks up = share of its spans with X_end > X_start; the rows of a log-growth difference (rule A − rule B) add up to the whole-window difference ln(NAV_A,end) − ln(NAV_B,end). X: the parent = hold-the-parent at 0 bps; an index = its price; GOLDBEES = its close; cash = the LBES level; a rule = its NAV at 20.8 bps.

ksplit

-all minus -idx by k: for each B stretch, d_b = ret(b-all) − ret(b-idx) over the stretch's span (b = 50 or 80, the ledger's all_minus_idx_50 / _80); the figure for k = 0 (or 1, 2) is the plain sum of d_b over the stretches whose B has that k; k >= 1 = the sum over the k = 1 and k = 2 stretches; weeks = the OUT-SELL weekly decisions in those stretches; a simple sum of period returns, not a compounded figure, and not a statement of which of the two differences between -all and -idx (holding indices that are on SELL, or the 1/4 weights) causes it

cmix

constant mix at a rule's own averages: each line's share = the mean over the weekly decisions of the rule's target share (f_parent, f_goldbees, f_cash, f_index), rebalanced at every decision and every basket change; shows how much of a difference is only a different average exposure. eq3_index_basket = one third each of Nifty 100, Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100, rebalanced at every weekly decision, 20.8 bps, nothing else

state

sessions held in a state = the sessions of the book's calendar whose held target is that regime (and, in OUT-SELL, that k): a decision's target is held from the close of its trade session (the next session after the decision), T0's target from the first session

r4

R4, leave one spell out: for OUT-SELL spell s, a run in which -all holds 100% cash (as -liq) on spell s's decisions and its own target everywhere else; C1-C6 recomputed with the run's -all against the headline's comparators (-orig, -liq, -half, -idx); 'flips' = the comparisons whose PASS / FAIL differs from the headline's

r5

R5: every index OHLC4 and close of session i is multiplied by (1 − 0.005 ÷ 252)^i (i counted in sessions of the window's calendar from T0), a fund-cost drag of 0.5 pp a year on the index leg; dividends (the opposite side) are not run; R2: LIQUIDCASE as the cash leg (W1 whole window; W2 from 2024-01-24); R3: W1 from 2015-01-02, W2 live decisions from 2021-11-01, each starting in its own first state

Reproduce

From AA/: bash tests/T16/run.sh regenerates the evidence, the gates, analysis.log, this page and its check (python tests/T16/report.py --run headline, then python tests/T16/check_page.py --run headline, which re-derives every number and every date on this page from the raw evidence files and exits 1 on any failure). No draws are made and no seed is used.
